items.title: The National | Hegseth reportedly moves to restrict defence ties
items.summary_auto: Nov. 22, 2026 | U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth reportedly issues a memo restricting defence ties with Canada. A father and daughter arrested by ICE at a Seattle airport draws backlash. And Go Public investigates a man's fight against AI customer service.

items.title: Carney, opposition leaders trade comedic jabs at press gallery dinner
items.summary_auto: Two Mark Carneys and a Donald Trump shared the stage at the Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner Saturday, when the prime minister got a little help from This Hour Has 22 Minutes impersonators to give the traditional comedic speech.

items.title: FULL SPEECH | Carney roasts opposition, Trump at press gallery dinner
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a few jabs at his fellow politicians, journalists and U.S. President Donald Trump at the annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner in Ottawa on Saturday. 'This is a tough room. And I've been in the Oval Office, alone, with its new interior decorator,' Carney said, in an apparent poke at the U.S. leader. (Raw, unedited speech)

items.title: First Nations leader warns of 'dire' consequences if B.C. repeals the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act
items.summary_auto: British Columbia's new Conservative government could face "dire" consequences if they repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act as promised, a First Nations leader said, adding that he's willing to work with new Premier Lorne Doerkson.

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse after member states reject deal for not mentioning fossil fuels
Pay halted for suspended Vancouver police officer charged with fraud and theft
items.summary_auto: The Vancouver Police Board has discontinued pay for a high-profile officer accused of fraud and theft.

items.title: UN-affiliated athlete swims in dangerous Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's impact on wildlife
items.summary_auto: Lewis Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days last week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how Iran war threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

items.title: Trump calling Putin a friend is 'appalling,' says former ambassador to NATO
items.summary_auto: Kurt Volker, former U.S. Ambassador to NATO, tells CBC's Rosemary Barton that it’s 'appalling' to hear U.S. President Donald Trump double down on calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his 'friend.' Volker also weighs in on the leaked classified Pentagon memo about restricting defence ties with Canada.

items.title: A small latte and a chat, please: Why this B.C. café owner put conversation on the menu
items.summary_auto: Registered clinical counsellor Shane Trudell estimates one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but many people aren't aware of it. A New Westminster café hopes to help.

items.title: Miley Cyrus weds Maxx Morando in California, People magazine reports
items.summary_auto: Grammy-winning pop star Miley Cyrus married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx ‌Morando, in California on Saturday, People magazine and other U.S. entertainment news ​outlets reported.

items.title: Fire at Indonesian candy factory leaves 3 dead, dozens of workers missing
items.summary_auto: A fire swept through a candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province Saturday, leaving three people dead and rescue teams searching for 36 workers who remained unaccounted for, officials said.

items.title: Elite B.C. snowboarder's injury highlights financial strain of Olympic dreams
items.summary_auto: Prince George's Meryeta O'Dine suffered fractured ankle in a devastating crash during a snowboard cross training run in February and was unable to compete at the 2026 Olympics.

items.title: B.C. couple lose business in devastating fire, credit volunteer firefighters with saving their home
items.summary_auto: A West Kootenay couple is counting their blessings after a massive fire destroyed their home-based mechanic shop in Burton, B.C. — and came dangerously close to taking their house with it.

items.title: Frustrated? Angry? Why these Nova Scotians say you should scream it out
items.summary_auto: A group of Nova Scotians now meet weekly to scream their frustrations into the ocean. From grocery prices to global instability, they say there's plenty to motivate them these days.

items.title: Was mispronouncing ‘Newfoundland’ the motive for murder?
items.summary_auto: If you’re from Newfoundland, perhaps you’ve wanted to murder someone over their mangled pronunciation of the place’s name. But it really happened one Friday night in 1876. Author and cultural historian Ainsley Hawthorne tells this tale to die for.

items.title: Quebecor CEO defends Telus bid, cites falling wireless prices and Canada's sovereignty
How a rainy afternoon in Montreal inspired an iconic Canadian board game
items.summary_auto: The bestselling Canadian board game of all time has sold more than 100 million copies worldwide, in 17 different languages. On the game's 45th anniversary, co-creator John Haney offers a personal account of the game's creation in his new book, My Trivial Pursuits: The Inside Story of the Board Game That Conquered the World.

items.title: Will Canadian workers refuse to handle Israeli goods? Why unions increasingly say they should
items.summary_auto: A movement to cut off Israeli goods is spreading across Canada's unions. The Canadian Labour Congress, which represents more than 3 million workers, passed a resolution last month declaring trade, services and relationships with Israel to be “hot cargo,"  emphasizing a call for workers  to refuse to handle weapons and military equipment destined for Israel.

items.title: Why the U.S. midterms might have ended JD Vance's presidential hopes
items.summary_auto: Vice-President JD Vance's presidential ambitions for 2028 could be among the more significant political casualties of the Democratic blue wave in this month's midterm elections.

items.title: WhatsApp is a 'lifeline' for refugees. Advocates fear it could be severed in fight over federal bill
items.summary_auto: Meta said this week that Bill C-22 could force it to "consider" withdrawing encrypted services like WhatsApp from Canada. Rights advocates say that would cut refugees and other newcomers off from a key platform they rely on to get information and stay connected to relatives back home.

items.title: Hudson, Que., community brings landmark church back to life after massive fire in 2024
items.summary_auto: More than two and a half years after a fire ripped through the historic St. James Church, work continues to bring it back to its former glory — but with a twist. The new space will serve not just as a church, but as a multipurpose community and cultural centre.
